nodes.name: Electrodeposition and anodic oxidation
nodes.procedure: Co(OH)_x nanosheets enriched with CoOOH were grown on carbon cloth (CC) by electrochemical deposition followed by in situ anodic oxidation.
nodes.source_text: Co(OH)_x nanosheets enriched with CoOOH were grown on carbon cloth (CC) by electrochemical deposition followed by in situ anodic oxidation.

nodes.name: Impregnation of Ru precursor
nodes.procedure: RuCl3 was introduced through impregnation onto Co(OH)_x/CC as the Ru source.
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, RuCl3 was introduced through impregnation as the Ru source

nodes.name: Laser irradiation synthesis
nodes.procedure: Laser irradiation was applied to Co(OH)_x nanosheets preloaded with RuCl3 on carbon cloth. The laser irradiation induces a localized thermal effect with fast heating and quenching, which simultaneously generates uniformly dispersed oxygen vacancies (OVs) on Co(OH)_x nanosheets and forms ultrafine Ru clusters that are directly anchored at the OVs.

nodes.characterization_summary: L-Ru/Co(OH)_x shows prominent diffraction peaks at 38.2°, 42.5°, and 43.8° indexed to CoOOH (JCPDS No. 26-0480) along with peaks from Co(OH)_2 (JCPDS No. 74-1057) at 38.2°, 58.2°, and 69.6°; no peaks corresponding to metallic Ru detected due to ultrasmall size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2b, the Co(OH)_x exhibits no obvious diffraction peaks except for the CC substrate... no peaks corresponding to metallic Ru were detected in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x, likely due to the ultrasmall size of the Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: L-Ru/Co(OH)_x and Co(OH)_x display peaks at 188, 467, 509, and 669 cm⁻¹; 188 cm⁻¹ corresponds to F_{2g} in Co(OH)_2 phase, latter three to Co-O(H) bond, E_g vibrations and A_{1g} modes in CoOOH; additional peak at 610 cm⁻¹ corresponds to A_{1g} of Ru-O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both L-Ru/Co(OH)_x and Co(OH)_x display four strong peaks at 188, 467, 509, and 669 cm^{-1}. The 188 cm^{-1} peak corresponds to the F_{2g} in Co(OH)_2 phase... a peak at 610 cm^{-1}, corresponding to A_{1g} of Ru-O, is observed in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x.

nodes.characterization_summary: L-Ru/Co(OH)_x presents morphology of nanosheet arrays tightly encapsulating carbon fibers in CC substrate, maintaining arrayed structure of Co(OH)_x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The L-Ru/Co(OH)_x presents the morphology of nanosheet arrays tightly encapsulating the carbon fibers in the CC substrate, where the arrayed structure of the Co(OH)_x is well maintained.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru clusters in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x highly dispersed on Co(OH)_x nanosheets surface with average size of 1.4 nm; lattice spacing of 0.23 nm matches (100) plane of Ru, additional spacings consistent with (101) and (002) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru clusters for L-Ru/Co(OH)_x were found to be highly dispersed on the surface of Co(OH)_x nanosheets with an average size of about 1.4 nm... A lattice spacing of 0.23 nm in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x matches the (100) plane of Ru.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of Ru is determined to be about 10.8 at.% and the mass loading of Ru is 0.05 mg cm^{-2} via inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS).

nodes.characterization_summary: L-Ru/Co(OH)_x shows strongest intensity of oxygen vacancies reflected from g = 2.0013.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the EPR spectra (Figure 3a), L-Ru/Co(OH)_x shows the strongest intensity of OVs reflected from g = 2.0013.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS of L-Ru/Co(OH)_x, W-Ru/Co(OH)_x, and Co(OH)_x shows peaks at 529.8 eV (Co-O), 530.7 eV (Co-OH), 531.8 eV (OV), 532.9 eV (chemisorbed water); OV content 31.7% (L-Ru/Co(OH)_x), 18.1% (W-Ru/Co(OH)_x), 16.9% (Co(OH)_x). Ru 3p peaks blue-shifted 0.7 eV (L-Ru/Co(OH)_x) and 0.3 eV (W-Ru/Co(OH)_x) vs Ru/C indicating electron-rich Ru. Co 2p shows Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio increases to 3.4 in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3b exhibits the O 1s XPS spectra of L-Ru/Co(OH)_x, W-Ru/Co(OH)_x, and Co(OH)_x, where four peaks located at 529.8, 530.7, 531.8, and 532.9 eV, corresponding to the Co-O, Co-OH, OV, and chemisorbed water... The peak area proportion of OVs in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x was calculated to be approximately 31.7%, substantially higher than that in W-Ru/Co(OH)_x (18.1%) and Co(OH)_x (16.9%)... the peak area ratio of Co²⁺/Co³⁺ for L-Ru/Co(OH)_x increases to 3.4

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows L-Ru/Co(OH)_x close to Ru foil with shift to lower energy vs W-Ru/Co(OH)_x indicating electron-rich Ru; Co K-edge shows slight shift to lower energy. Ru K-edge EXAFS shows Ru-Ru coordination at 2.36 Å and Ru-O at 1.50 Å, no RuO₂ peak at 3.22 Å; WT shows Ru-Ru at 9.3 Å. Co K-edge EXAFS shows Co-O at 1.50 Å and Co-Co/Ru at 2.45 Å; Co-O coordination number 1.48 in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x vs 3.74 in W-Ru/Co(OH)_x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform (FT) k³-weighted χ(k)-function for the Ru K-edge EXAFS spectrum of L-Ru/Co(OH)_x shows a strong peak near 2.36 Å... The FT of the Co K-edge oscillation displays two main peaks located at ∼1.50 and ∼2.45 Å... the fitted coordination number (CN) of Co-O in L-Ru/Co(OH)_x is 1.48, lower than W-Ru/Co(OH)_x (3.74).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman on L-Ru/Co(OH)_x shows no Ru-H peak (~820 cm⁻¹) accumulation at cathodic potentials, indicating rapid H* spillover from Ru to support; Co-O modes disappear upon potential application.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for L-Ru/Co(OH)_x, the characteristic Co-O vibrational modes from Co(OH)_x appear at the OCP... These peaks completely disappear upon the application of a cathodic potential, and no Ru-H-related peaks are observed, indicating the absence of H* intermediate accumulation on the Ru sites.
